backendEnablerProposals.uiNeed: A reader with no account who does not want an identity provider has no way in. Today the only lanes that create a member are Google and GitHub; the credential lane can only reach an account that already exists.
backendEnablerProposals.productStatement: The owner settled it on 2026-08-13: an academy member account belongs to the EXPERT's users and has nothing to do with nivo. An academy that cannot register its own users is missing a capability, not exercising a design choice. The entry page therefore carries both lanes, and this mutation is what makes the sign-up lane real.
backendEnablerProposals.operation: signUp(input: SignUpInput!): SignUpResponse!  — on the ACADEMY API (:3069), mirroring the control plane's existing resolver at src/features/core/api/core/graphql/mutations/auth/sign-up/
evidence: 52 academy mutations dumped unfiltered: signIn, signOut, exchangeOauthCode, refreshSession — and no signUp
createMember exists but sits beside setMemberRole / setMemberStatus / removeMember, so it is the owner adding a member, not a stranger registering
the academy's own copy catalogue already carries entry.signUp.{title,body,submit,switchPrompt,switchAction} — copied from starci, where the capability does exist
auth.e2e-spec.ts:233 / :293 — both existing lanes already create a member on a brand-new identity, so the member-creation path this would reuse is proven
backendEnablerProposals.authorization: public, like signIn and exchangeOauthCode. It creates the Keycloak user and upserts the local member, so it must refuse an existing email the same way it refuses bad credentials — without disclosing which case it was.
backendEnablerProposals.compatibility: purely additive; no existing operation changes shape. The FE keeps working unchanged until the mutation exists.
backendEnablerProposals.tests: a brand-new email creates member role=member status=active and sets the refresh cookie; an email already registered is refused without disclosing existence and without upserting; a weak password is refused by Keycloak policy and reported without leaking the policy internals
backendEnablerProposals.escalationTrigger: the moment a customer asks for email sign-up on their academy, or the entry page is asked to show a Đăng ký affordance that does anything

backendEnablerProposals.uiNeed: A member who signed up by password and forgot it is locked out permanently. The entry page cannot offer 'Quên mật khẩu?' because there is nothing behind it.
backendEnablerProposals.operation: requestPasswordReset(input) and resetPassword(input) on the ACADEMY API, mirroring src/features/core/api/core/graphql/mutations/auth/{request-password-reset,reset-password}/
evidence: neither resolver exists under src/features/expert/graphql/mutations/auth/, which holds exactly four
the academy catalogue already carries entry.signIn.switchPrompt = 'Quên mật khẩu?' and entry.resetSent — copy without a capability behind it
the control plane's reset flow is already built and already proves the response must not disclose whether an account exists
backendEnablerProposals.authorization: public. The response must be identical whether or not the address is registered — the control plane's e2e already fixes that rule and this must not weaken it.
backendEnablerProposals.tests: an unknown address returns the same response as a known one; a used token is refused; an expired token is refused; a successful reset invalidates existing sessions
backendEnablerProposals.escalationTrigger: the first support request from a member who cannot sign in, or academy-sign-up shipping — password sign-up without password recovery is a trap rather than a feature

backendEnablerProposals.uiNeed: A 'Ghi nhớ đăng nhập' control cannot be offered: the FE has no way to influence how long the session lasts.
backendEnablerProposals.operation: either a persist flag on SignInInput, or a shorter default refresh-cookie lifetime with an opt-in to the longer one
evidence: SignInInput is exactly { email, password }
the refresh cookie is set by the resolver, so the browser side cannot choose its lifetime
backendEnablerProposals.compatibility: additive if the flag is optional and the current lifetime stays the default
backendEnablerProposals.tests: the flag off yields a session that ends with the browser; on yields the long-lived cookie; the flag cannot lengthen a session beyond the configured maximum
backendEnablerProposals.escalationTrigger: only when someone decides what the two lifetimes should BE. Until then a checkbox would be a control that promises what nothing keeps, which is why the entry page does not draw one.
